title: Flotation Cell

introduction.definition: A mechanical flotation cell separates valuable mineral particles from waste. Reagents make the wanted mineral surfaces water-repellent. Air enters down a hollow shaft and a spinning rotor–stator breaks it into fine bubbles; the hydrophobic particles attach to the bubbles and rise into a froth, which overflows into the launder as concentrate.
applications: Copper, lead, zinc, gold and phosphate concentration
key_points: Rotor suspends solids and disperses air
Froth depth and air rate control grade/recovery
Cells in banks: rougher, scavenger, cleaner
introduction.summary: A mechanical flotation cell separates valuable minerals from waste rock. Air is blown down a hollow shaft and dispersed into fine bubbles by a spinning rotor and stator. Particles made water-repellent by reagents attach to the bubbles and rise to form a froth that overflows into a launder; the rest leaves as tailings.

pressure.title: Hydrophobic vs hydrophilic particles
pressure.description: Collectors make the wanted mineral surfaces water-repellent (hydrophobic). Those particles attach to air bubbles and rise into the froth (red zone), which overflows into the launder as concentrate. Hydrophilic gangue stays in the pulp (blue) and leaves as tailings. Frothers stabilise the froth.

video_tutorials.title: Flotation Cell — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Flotation Cell.
A mechanical flotation cell separates valuable mineral particles from waste.
Reagents make the wanted mineral surfaces water-repellent.

Air enters down a hollow shaft and a spinning rotor–stator breaks it into fine bubbles; the hydrophobic particles attach to the bubbles and rise into a froth, which overflows into the launder as concentrate.
Typical applications include copper, lead, zinc, gold and phosphate concentration; coal fines cleaning; de-inking of paper pulp.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Rotor on Hollow Shaft (air enters through the shaft).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Flotation Cell works.
Conditioned pulp enters the cell.
Air flows down the hollow shaft.
Rotor and stator create fine bubbles.
Hydrophobic particles ride bubbles into the froth.
Froth overflows into the launder.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Collectors make the wanted mineral surfaces water-repellent (hydrophobic).

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flotation Cell.
Check froth, air flow and level.
Inspect rotor/stator wear.
Replace rotor/stator.
Watch for poor recovery: mineral in tailings. Common cause: wrong reagent dose, coarse particles, low air.
Watch for rotor wear: bubble size grows. Common cause: abrasion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
